title: Pattern recognition and a schematic catalog
stack: React 19 admin (workbench 03 base) · Project Builder CLI 0.9.11 on @pbuilder/sdk 0.12.0 · Claude Opus 5.5 headless in Docker
about: An agent works through ten small product changes on the same admin, one session per change, each starting from the repository the previous one left. Two patterns repeat: an optional Author field four times and a static page with its sidebar entry three times, with three one-off changes between them. Experiment 2 gives the agent the option to author schematics and observes whether, and when, it automates a pattern; it is pre-registered in harness/exp2/PROTOCOL.md and reported in results-recognition/. Experiment 3 compares doing the sequence by hand against having a catalog of reviewed schematics, two that fit the patterns and three working distractors, without being told which to use. A hidden checker scores every change.
proves: Whether an agent notices a repeated pattern and automates it unprompted, and whether a ready catalog of schematics, with distractors, makes small repeated changes cheaper than writing them by hand.

experiments.title: Schematic catalog with distractors against by hand
experiments.hypothesis: With a catalog of reviewed schematics, two that fit the repeated changes and three distractors, and no instruction on which to use, the median cost or the median total tokens per task falls by at least 30% against writing every change by hand, at no worse correctness.
experiments.variable: Whether the repository has the catalog registered (harness/exp3/catalog) and the pbuilder skill, or neither and no builder binary. The base, the ten prompts, their order and the model are the same.
constants: Workbench 03 base; prompts harness/tasks/T01 to T10 in sequence.json order
One headless session per task, claude -p --bare, one container per sequence, repository carried over and committed between sessions
Sequences sequential, never in parallel; arm order alternates per sequence
3 sequences per arm, 30 sessions per arm
Correctness scored by harness/checker/check-task.sh, outside the agent

recorded_checks.source: harness/checker/check-task.sh (30/30 sessions correct in each arm, no regressions)
results-selection.json (21/21 pattern tasks used the right schematic, 0 distractor uses, 0 misses)

experiments.interpretation: Not supported: median cost per task fell 16% with the catalog ($0.147 against $0.175) and median tokens 1%, short of 30%; total cost over the 30 sessions fell 13% ($5.57 against $6.38). The agent picked the right schematic on every pattern task and never used a distractor. The saving sits in the optional Author field (median $0.27 against $0.32 per task); the static page is so cheap by hand that reading the catalog costs more tokens than the schematic saves, and the one-off tasks dilute the median.
